details: Bitcoin spot ETFs recorded a net inflow of $298 million on August 17th, reversing recent outflows. BlackRock's IBIT led with $160 million, bringing its historical total to over $61 billion. Fidelity's FBTC also saw a significant inflow of $112 million.
title: Bitcoin Spot ETFs See $298M Inflow, BlackRock Leads

details: Institutional investors are increasingly favoring Ethereum, with U.S. spot ETH ETFs recording approximately $2.85 billion in net inflows last week. This marks a new record high for ETH ETFs, significantly surpassing the roughly $548 million recorded by spot BTC ETFs over the same period.
title: Institutional Capital Shifts to ETH ETFs with Record Inflows

details: A record 41 million ETH, representing 34.4% of the total supply, is now locked in staking contracts, removing a substantial amount from active trading. This growing illiquidity could amplify price movements. Additionally, Bitmine has increased its Ethereum treasury to approximately $11 billion.
title: Record 34.4% of ETH Supply Locked in Staking Contracts

details: The next significant Ethereum upgrade, codenamed "Glamsterdam," has reportedly been delayed to the fourth quarter of 2026. This upgrade is intended to enhance Layer 1 execution capacity and block-building efficiency for the network.
title: Ethereum's Major 'Glamsterdam' Upgrade Pushed to Late 2026

details: Bitcoin remains capped below $64,000, with the broader crypto market capitalization around $2.17 trillion. The market is being influenced by the expiration of the U.S.–Iran ceasefire agreement and anticipation of upcoming Federal Reserve FOMC minutes, which could provide clues on future interest rate policies.
title: Bitcoin Stays Below $64K Amid Geopolitical and Macro Factors

details: Hashdex's DEFI spot Bitcoin ETF ceased trading and initiated liquidation on August 17th. This marks the first closure of a U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF, a development attributed to reduced investor inflows and heightened competition within the market.
title: Hashdex's DEFI Becomes First U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETF to Close

details: The Insolvency Service and Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) have issued a warning following reports of investors losing hundreds of thousands of pounds to a "Ponzi-style" crypto scheme called Key Coin Assets Ltd. The company allegedly promised high returns but showed no evidence of genuine trading, with funds being diverted to personal accounts.
title: Investors Warned After Losing £300K in "Ponzi-Style" Crypto Scheme
